title: Prior notification of a concentration (Case M.12430 – TOYOTA / VOLVO / DAIMLER TRUCK / CELLCENTRIC)
content: Prior notification of a concentration (Case M.12430 – TOYOTA / VOLVO / DAIMLER TRUCK / CELLCENTRIC) (Text with EEA relevance) (C/2026/6254) 1. On 16 November 2026, the Commission received notification of a proposed concentration pursuant to Article 4 of Council Regulation (EC) No 139/2004 (1). This notification concerns the following undertakings: — Daimler Truck AG (‘Daimler Truck’, Germany), controlled by Daimler Truck Holding AG (Germany), — Aktiebolaget Volvo (‘Volvo’, Sweden), — Toyota Motor Corporation (‘Toyota’, Japan), — cellcentric GmbH & Co. KG (‘cellcentric’, Germany), currently controlled by Daimler Truck and Volvo. Daimler Truck, Volvo and Toyota will acquire within the meaning of Articles 3(1)(b) and 3(4) of the Merger Regulation joint control of cellcentric. The concentration is accomplished by way of purchase of shares. 2. The business activities of the undertakings concerned are the following: — Daimler Truck is a publicly listed company that is active globally in the production and sale of medium and heavy- duty commercial vehicles, including trucks and buses, as well as industrial engines and selected financial services, — Volvo is a publicly listed company that is active globally in the production and sale of on- and off-highway trucks, buses, construction equipment, marine engines, industrial engines for off-road and power generation applications, as well as engines for on-highway vehicles, — Toyota is a publicly listed multinational automotive manufacturer active globally in the production and supply of passenger cars ranging from compact cars to SUVs, pickups and buses. It also develops fuel cell technology, including for passenger-car and heavy-duty applications, — cellcentric develops, produces, and commercializes hydrogen fuel cell systems for use in heavy-duty commercial vehicles and other applications. 3. On preliminary examination, the Commission finds that the notified transaction could fall within the scope of the Merger Regulation. However, the final decision on this point is reserved. 4. The Commission invites interested third parties to submit their possible observations on the proposed concentration to the Commission. Observations must reach the Commission not later than 10 days following the date of this publication.
